terms.gloss: a spring; the source of a river, and of anything
evidence: Ov. Rem. 97: dē magnīs fontibus orta
Cic. de Or. 1.42: ab illō fonte et capite Sōcrate
Varr. LL 5.92: ā pāstōribus enim hōrum vocābulōrum orīgō
Hor. C. 4.14.45: fontium quī cēlat orīginēs Nīlus (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: the source of a river; the fountainhead

phrases.latin: flūmina pauca vidēs dē magnīs fontibus orta: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs
phrases.english: you see few rivers that rise from great sources: most grow by gathering waters

phrases.latin: urgērent praetereā philosophōrum gregēs jam ab illō fonte et capite Sōcrate
phrases.english: and then the flocks of philosophers would press you, all of them from Socrates on, the fountainhead and source

sources: Lewis & Short: fons · Lewis & Short: origo · Lewis & Short: caput
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 383.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. source (of river); source, origin.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-ovidius, loci-varro), checked against the editions named there. Cicero, De oratore 1, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
